newsitem.title: USA: Early holiday results depress U.S. retail stocks.
newsitem.headline: Early holiday results depress U.S. retail stocks.

text.p: Shares in most big U.S. retailers slid Thursday in reaction to disappointing, but still inconclusive, early reports on the crucial holiday sales season, as well as a generally weak stock market.

J.C. Penney Co Inc was off 1-1/2 to 47-1/4 after it said it expects fourth-quarter earnings before charges will not meet Wall Street expectations and that profit margins for November and December were below planned levels.
Dayton Hudson Corp said Thursday holiday sales in its discount stores were on plan but were below expectations in its department stores. Its shares were off 1-7/8 to 37-3/8.

Carson Pirie Scott & Co reported holiday same-store sales for the four weeks ended December 28 were up, in line with expectations. But it said it expects same-store sales for the standard five-week period ending December 30 to be slightly below year-ago levels. Shares in the Milwaukee-based retailer were off 3/8 to 24-7/8.
These and other prelimary holiday results are "further confirmation that the holiday was one of moderate growth," said Morgan Stanley retailing analyst Bruce Missett.
Sears Roebuck & Co was off 1-1/8 to 45, while May Department Stores Co was off 1-1/4 to 45-1/2.
The Dow Jones industrial average was off more than 72 toward mid-morning.
Shares in computer specialty retailer CompUSA Inc were off 4-1/4 to 16-3/8.

On December 27, Nordstrom Inc said holiday sales in its stores open for more than a year fell moderately versus last year and that earnings for the quarter ending January 31 would be below Wall Street expectations.

"I wouldn't use Nordstrom or Penney as a snapshot of the industry," said Prudential Securities analyst Wayne Hood, who added he expects Sears, May and Federated Department Stores Inc, whose shares were off 3/4 to 30-1/8, to report results in line with expectations or slightly better.
